answer: An farming party who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the pigment history. Churn is counted in quartz, and grove publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 20% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 221 account operation therefore ties up 16 million dollars of idle capital. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
